job.summary: Plan generated and independently checked. Read the findings before assignment.

content.title: IT Role Onboarding Plan
content.summary: This onboarding plan for the IT role ensures compliance with mandatory policies and encourages good practices within the first 30 days. It includes acknowledgement of the employee handbook, protocols for unexpected absences, early readiness reviews by managers, and optional archive review activities.

items.source_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
items.learning_objective: Ensure all new IT employees acknowledge the current employee handbook within 1 working day of joining to understand company policies and expectations.
items.practical_activity: Simulate accessing and digitally acknowledging the employee handbook in the HR system or completing supervised paper acknowledgement if digital access is unavailable.
items.lesson: It is mandatory for all employees to acknowledge the current employee handbook within 1 working day of joining the company. This process ensures you understand essential policies and workplace expectations. If digital access is unavailable during this period, HR will record this outage and provide a supervised paper version for acknowledgement within the same 1 working day timeframe.
checklist: Locate the employee handbook in the online portal or via HR.
Confirm access to the handbook on Day 1.
Complete digital acknowledgement or supervised paper acknowledgement if needed.
Report any access issues immediately to HR.

scenario.prompt: You joined this morning and want to comply with the handbook acknowledgement requirement but find the online portal is down.
scenario.expected_response: Report the access issue to HR promptly and complete the supervised paper acknowledgement form that HR provides within the same working day to comply with the handbook acknowledgement requirement.

quiz.question: What must an employee do regarding the employee handbook within 1 working day of joining?
options: Acknowledge the current employee handbook, digitally or via supervised paper if access is unavailable
Read the employee handbook but acknowledgement is optional
Wait until the end of the first week to acknowledge the handbook
Only acknowledge the handbook if requested by the manager
quiz.explanation: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

rubric.criterion: Timely completion of handbook acknowledgement within 1 working day
Correct procedure followed when access to handbook is unavailable
Demonstrated understanding during the practical acknowledgement activity

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
items.learning_objective: Understand and execute the proper notification process for emergencies preventing attendance at work to maintain clear communication and compliance.
items.practical_activity: Role-play a scenario where an unexpected emergency prevents attendance at work and practice notifying the manager promptly; also simulate HR notification from a nominated contact when the employee cannot communicate.
items.lesson: If an emergency prevents you from attending work, you must notify your manager as soon as reasonably possible to ensure they are informed promptly. If you are unable to communicate directly, a nominated contact can notify HR, who will record the circumstances. This procedure helps maintain clear communication and timely awareness of your situation.
checklist: Identify and note your manager's contact details.
Notify your manager immediately if you cannot attend due to an emergency.
If unable to communicate, ensure a nominated contact informs HR.
Verify HR records the notification and circumstances.

scenario.prompt: You suddenly become ill on the morning of work and cannot inform your manager yourself.
scenario.expected_response: Your nominated emergency contact calls HR to notify them of your absence and the circumstances. HR records the notification accordingly, ensuring your manager is informed as soon as possible.

quiz.question: What should you do if an emergency prevents your attendance and you cannot communicate with your manager?
options: Ensure a nominated contact notifies HR who records the circumstances
Wait until you can contact the manager yourself
Do not inform anyone if you cannot contact the manager
Ask a colleague to inform your manager without involving HR
quiz.explanation: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

rubric.criterion: Prompt notification to manager or HR via nominated contact
Correct use of nominated contact notification procedure
Accurate documentation of notification circumstances in practical activity

items.source_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
items.learning_objective: Prepare to participate in and understand the importance of readiness reviews conducted by your manager within the first 30 calendar days.
items.practical_activity: Simulate a readiness review discussion with your manager, identifying your current skill gaps, supervised-work limits, and setting follow-up dates for development.
items.lesson: Within your first 30 calendar days, your manager will review your readiness for your role. They will document any remaining knowledge or skill gaps, any limits on supervised work you require, and establish dates for follow-up training or assessments. This process helps ensure you receive appropriate guidance and support during onboarding.
checklist: Prepare a list of skills and tasks you have learned.
Discuss any remaining challenges or gaps with your manager.
Review any supervised-work limitations assigned.
Agree on follow-up dates for further training or review.

scenario.prompt: Your manager schedules a readiness review to discuss your progress after three weeks on the job.
scenario.expected_response: You discuss your current abilities, note any gaps or difficulties, confirm limits on tasks you can perform under supervision, and agree on dates for follow-up training and evaluations.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the manager’s readiness review by the end of the first 30 days?
options: To document gaps, supervised-work limits, and schedule follow-ups
To finalize a promotion decision
To complete exit paperwork
To assign permanent tasks without support
quiz.explanation: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
quiz.evidence_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

rubric.criterion: Active participation in readiness review discussion
Accurate identification of gaps and supervised-work limits
Agreement on clear and realistic follow-up plans

items.source_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
items.learning_objective: Recognize the importance of regularly reviewing archive searchability and proactively suggest improvements to enhance document retrieval.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a mock quarterly review of the archive system’s search functions and draft recommendations for better naming conventions or indexing strategies.
items.lesson: Although not mandatory, record owners are encouraged to regularly review the archive’s searchability every quarter. Improving naming conventions and indexing helps make document retrieval faster and more efficient. Taking initiative to propose these improvements supports overall technology and knowledge management goals within the organization.
checklist: Review current archive naming conventions and indexing.
Test search functionality and note any difficulties.
Identify potential improvements for naming or indexing.
Draft and submit proposals for recommended improvements.

scenario.prompt: As an IT team member, you notice the archive search returns inconsistent results.
scenario.expected_response: You conduct a detailed review of the archive search functionality, note issues with naming and indexing, and propose actionable improvements to enhance search consistency and efficiency.

quiz.question: What are record owners encouraged to do quarterly regarding archive records?
options: Review archive searchability and propose improvements
Delete outdated records
Ignore archive records to focus on current tasks
Limit access to the archive system
quiz.explanation: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
quiz.evidence_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

rubric.criterion: Thoroughness of archive search review
Quality and relevance of proposed improvements
Clarity and feasibility of improvement proposal document

items.source_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
items.module_title: Using the Approved Repository for Operational Evidence
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply the policy for storing operational evidence only within approved repositories to ensure compliance and record integrity.
items.practical_activity: Simulate uploading a sample decision record to the approved document repository and verify that no local copy is the sole record.
items.lesson: All operational evidence, such as decisions and transaction records, must be stored in the approved case or document repository. Keeping only a local copy is not allowed, as it poses risks of data loss or incomplete records. Using the approved repository preserves integrity, enables audit trails, and ensures consistent access across relevant teams.
checklist: Locate the company's approved document repository system.
Upload a test operational record to the repository.
Verify that no local copy is considered the sole record.
Ensure access permissions are correctly set according to guidelines.

scenario.prompt: You completed a key decision for a client case and saved it locally on your computer. What should you do to comply with company policy?
scenario.expected_response: You must upload the decision record to the approved document repository immediately, ensuring the local copy is not the only record and the operational evidence is properly stored.

quiz.question: According to company policy, where must operational evidence be stored?
options: In the approved case or document repository
On your local computer only
Sent via email to your manager
In a personal cloud storage
quiz.explanation: The policy states that employees must store operational evidence in the approved repository. A local copy must not be the sole record to ensure data integrity and accessibility.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies the approved repository as the required location
Explains why local copies alone are insufficient
Demonstrates practical ability to upload a document in the simulated activity

items.source_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
items.learning_objective: Recognize accidental data disclosures and apply immediate reporting and evidence preservation procedures.
items.practical_activity: Review a scenario of an accidental file transfer and practice reporting it through the POL-09 process, documenting evidence without deletion.
items.lesson: If you notice data being transferred unintentionally, you must stop it if possible and report the suspected disclosure immediately using the POL-09 procedure. Preserving all evidence is mandatory, and deleting or concealing incident history is prohibited. Timely and transparent reporting protects company assets and helps remediate issues quickly.
checklist: Recognize signs of unintended data transfer.
Attempt to stop the transfer when feasible.
Report the incident immediately through POL-09.
Preserve all related evidence without alteration or deletion.

scenario.prompt: You realize you accidentally sent confidential information to the wrong email group. What steps do you take following company policy?
scenario.expected_response: Stop further sending if possible, report the accidental disclosure immediately through POL-09, preserve all evidence related to the incident, and do not delete any history silently.

quiz.question: What must you do if you suspect an accidental data disclosure?
options: Report immediately through POL-09 and preserve evidence
Ignore if it seems minor
Delete incident history to protect privacy
Wait to see if a manager notices
quiz.explanation: The policy requires immediate reporting of suspected disclosures through POL-09 and preservation of evidence. Concealing or deleting incident history is not allowed.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

rubric.criterion: Demonstrates correct identification and stopping of accidental transfer
Accurately follows the POL-09 reporting procedure
Maintains evidence without alteration or deletion in activity

items.source_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
items.learning_objective: Understand respectful communication standards and proper procedures for reporting misconduct confidentially.
items.practical_activity: Role-play a scenario involving overhearing workplace harassment and practice confidentially reporting concerns via the HR channel.
items.lesson: All employees are required to communicate respectfully and avoid harassment, threats, or discrimination. Witnesses to concerning behavior should report issues through the confidential HR channel and avoid sharing allegations with other colleagues. This approach fosters a safe, respectful workplace and protects privacy.
checklist: Use respectful language in all work communications.
Recognize behaviors that constitute harassment, threats, or discrimination.
If witnessing misconduct, report it confidentially to HR immediately.
Do not circulate allegations among coworkers to maintain discretion.

scenario.prompt: You overhear a colleague making discriminating remarks about another employee. How do you proceed according to policy?
scenario.expected_response: You report your concerns confidentially to HR through the designated channel without discussing the allegation with other colleagues.

quiz.question: If you witness harassment, what is the correct reporting procedure?
options: Report confidentially to HR channel without circulating the allegation
Tell your team to watch out for the person
Ignore it if not directly involved
Confront the harasser publicly
quiz.explanation: The policy requires confidential reporting to HR without spreading the allegations to others, ensuring respect and privacy are maintained.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

rubric.criterion: Explains respectful communication requirements
Demonstrates confidential reporting following policy
Practices discretion by not circulating allegations

items.source_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
items.learning_objective: Achieve at least 80% on mandatory knowledge assessments through effective study and retake strategies as needed.
items.practical_activity: Complete a practice knowledge test covering key policies, review incorrect answers, and retake the assessment to meet passing criteria.
items.lesson: All employees must achieve a minimum score of 80% on mandatory knowledge assessments. If the first attempt is unsuccessful, targeted revision is required before another attempt. The initial assessment result remains recorded to ensure accurate training records and compliance tracking.
checklist: Review training materials thoroughly before the assessment.
Attempt the knowledge test with focus.
If score is below 80%, identify weak areas and revise.
Retake the test until scoring at least 80%.
Ensure all scores are recorded appropriately.

scenario.prompt: You scored 75% on your first knowledge assessment attempt. What are your next steps?
scenario.expected_response: Review the topics you missed, study targeted materials, then retake the assessment. The first result remains recorded, so continue until you score at least 80%.

quiz.question: What is required if you fail the initial mandatory assessment?
options: Revise targeted material and retake; original result remains recorded
You do not need to retake the test
You can delete the original score and try again fresh
Ask to skip the assessment
quiz.explanation: Employees must revise and attempt again after failing; the first result must still be recorded to maintain accurate records.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

rubric.criterion: Demonstrates understanding of assessment pass requirements
Completes revision and successful retake in activity
Keeps original attempt recorded as per policy

items.source_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
items.learning_objective: Understand the process and timing to request correction of inaccurate attendance and the role of HR in record retention.
items.practical_activity: Simulate discovering an inaccurate attendance entry and formally submit a correction request within 2 working days. Prepare a summary of what records HR retains in this process.
items.lesson: Employees are required to request a correction for any inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering the error. This prompt action ensures accuracy in attendance records. Additionally, HR retains the original attendance value along with evidence supporting the correction to maintain audit integrity. Adhering to these guidelines ensures compliance and helps keep accurate personnel records.
checklist: Identify an inaccurate attendance entry promptly.
Submit correction request within 2 working days of discovery.
Understand HR's role in retaining original values and supporting evidence.
Maintain records of correction request submission.

scenario.prompt: You notice that your attendance record incorrectly shows you arriving an hour late today. What steps do you take to correct this, and what does HR do with the original entry?
scenario.expected_response: I immediately submit a correction request to HR within 2 working days of discovering the error. HR retains the original attendance entry and keeps the evidence supporting the correction to ensure accurate record-keeping.

quiz.question: What is the maximum allowed time to request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry after discovering it?
options: 2 working days
5 working days
Immediately upon discovery
Within one week
quiz.explanation: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

rubric.criterion: Timeliness and accuracy of the correction request within the scenario
Completeness of the practical simulation of the correction request
Understanding HR's role as demonstrated in scenario and activity

items.source_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
items.learning_objective: Learn how document revisions should be linked and identified, and apply the correct document version according to the activity date.
items.practical_activity: Review a document revision history and link a new revision to its predecessor. Identify changed sections clearly and select the appropriate document version for a simulated activity date.
items.lesson: Document owners are responsible for linking each document revision to the previous version and clearly identifying any changed sections. Employees must use the document version that is effective on the date when they perform their activities, ensuring correct and up-to-date information is applied. Historical document versions remain accessible for audit purposes but should not be used for ongoing activities.
checklist: Verify linkage between current revision and superseded version.
Identify and highlight changed sections in the document revision.
Select the document version effective on the activity date.
Understand the availability of historical copies for audit only.

scenario.prompt: You receive a revised IT policy document for a task dated last week. How do you determine which version to use and how do you document the revision linkage?
scenario.expected_response: I verify that the document version is the one effective on the task date. I ensure that the revision links to the previous version and that all changed sections are identified per document control requirements.

quiz.question: Which document version should employees use for performing activities?
options: The version effective on the activity date
The most recent version regardless of date
The original version before any revisions
Any historical copy available
quiz.explanation: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
quiz.evidence_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

rubric.criterion: Correct identification and linkage of document revisions in scenario
Selection of proper document version for the activity date in scenario
Accuracy in practical activity linking and identification of changes

items.source_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
items.learning_objective: Understand the roles of the Operations Manager, Incident Lead, and IT during an incident for proper incident management and communication.
items.practical_activity: Simulate an incident scenario where you identify the appointment of an incident lead, record handover details, and define responsibilities for technical containment and business coordination.
items.lesson: During an incident, the duty Operations Manager must appoint a single incident lead and formally record the handover to ensure clear ownership. The IT team leads the technical containment efforts, addressing the technical impact of the incident, while the incident lead is responsible for coordinating business decisions and communications. This clear separation ensures effective incident management and communication flow.
checklist: Verify appointment of a single incident lead by Operations Manager.
Record details of handover and appointment.
Understand IT's role in technical containment.
Acknowledge incident lead's role in coordinating business decisions and communication.

scenario.prompt: In a cyberattack incident, who appoints the incident lead, and how are the roles of IT and incident lead separated?
scenario.expected_response: The duty Operations Manager appoints the incident lead and records the handover. IT leads technical containment measures, while the incident lead oversees business decisions and communicates with stakeholders.

quiz.question: Who is responsible for appointing the incident lead and what roles do IT and the incident lead play?
options: Operations Manager appoints; IT leads technical containment; incident lead manages business decisions and communications
IT appoints incident lead; incident lead handles technical containment; Operations Manager manages communications
Incident lead appoints themselves; IT handles business decisions; Operations Manager leads technical actions
Operations Manager handles all roles without appointment
quiz.explanation: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
quiz.evidence_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

rubric.criterion: Scenario response accuracy on appointment and role division
Completion of practical simulation of handover and role definition
Comprehension of incident management roles as shown in scenario and activity

items.source_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
items.learning_objective: Learn the required timeframe and conditions for deleting approved temporary customer-data exports and understand the impact of documented preservation holds.
items.practical_activity: Practice identifying an approved temporary customer-data export, note the task end time, and simulate deletion within 24 hours unless a preservation hold applies. Document how to verify preservation holds.
items.lesson: Employees must delete any approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends to protect customer data privacy. However, if a documented preservation hold is in place, deletion is suspended only for the specific records identified in that hold. It is crucial to follow these requirements to remain compliant and safeguard sensitive data properly.
checklist: Identify approved temporary customer-data exports.
Track approved task end time accurately.
Delete exports within 24 hours after task completion.
Check for and honor any documented preservation holds on specific records.

scenario.prompt: After completing a task involving temporary export of customer data, when and how should you delete the export? What if there is a preservation hold?
scenario.expected_response: I must delete the approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the task ends. If there is a documented preservation hold for certain records, I do not delete those records until the hold is lifted.

quiz.question: Within what time frame must approved temporary customer-data exports be deleted after task completion?
options: 24 elapsed hours
48 hours
Immediately after task ends
Within one week
quiz.explanation: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

rubric.criterion: Timeliness and accuracy of export deletion in scenario
Practical activity execution respecting deletion timeframe and holds
Understanding and application of preservation hold conditions

items.source_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
items.module_title: Completing Prerequisite Training for Restricted Tasks
items.learning_objective: Understand and complete all required prerequisite training before performing any restricted tasks independently.
items.practical_activity: Complete an assigned prerequisite training course on restricted IT tasks, followed by a supervised practical session with your manager. Document your completed training and supervised practice.
items.lesson: Employees must finish all prerequisite training before carrying out restricted tasks alone. While managers can provide supervised practice opportunities, they are not allowed to mark these prerequisites as complete unless the official training is fully completed. This ensures safety and compliance with company protocols, preventing errors due to incomplete preparation.
checklist: Identify all prerequisite training required for your restricted tasks.
Enroll in and complete the relevant training modules.
Arrange supervised practice sessions with your manager.
Keep records of completed training and supervised practice.

scenario.prompt: You are assigned a restricted system configuration task. Your manager asks if you can start immediately. How do you respond?
scenario.expected_response: Explain that you must first complete the required prerequisite training before independently performing the task. You can participate in supervised practice but cannot proceed alone until training is confirmed complete.

quiz.question: Before independently performing restricted tasks, what must employees do?
options: Complete the relevant prerequisite training.
Start supervised practice immediately.
Have the manager mark the prerequisite as complete.
Perform the task carefully without training.
quiz.explanation: Employees must complete relevant prerequisite training before performing restricted tasks independently, and supervised practice does not replace this requirement.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

rubric.criterion: Correctly explains prerequisite training requirements in scenario response.
Demonstrates completion of assigned training and supervised practice in practical activity.
Accurately identifies mandatory training completion in quiz.

items.source_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
items.learning_objective: Accurately assess parcel weight and route and request assistance when necessary according to safe-handling limits.
items.practical_activity: Simulate assessing several parcels of varying weights and routes. Determine when to request handling assistance as per posted limits. Record decisions and process used.
items.lesson: Before lifting any parcel, employees must assess its weight and the route to ensure safe handling. If the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded, they must request approved assistance. Importantly, employees should not assume a universal weight limit; each task requires specific assessment to avoid injury and maintain compliance.
checklist: Check the weight of the parcel using scales or provided data.
Evaluate the intended route for any obstacles or hazards.
Compare the parcel weight against the posted safe-handling limit.
Request handling assistance if the parcel exceeds the safe limit for solo lifting.

scenario.prompt: You find a parcel weighing 30kg to move along a cluttered corridor, with a posted safe-handling limit of 25kg. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: Assess the parcel weight and route, recognize the weight exceeds the safe limit, and request approved handling assistance before attempting to move the parcel.

quiz.question: What should employees do if a parcel exceeds the posted safe-handling limit?
options: Request approved handling assistance.
Lift the parcel carefully alone.
Ignore the limit if the parcel is small.
Invent a new universal limit for all parcels.
quiz.explanation: Employees must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded, and they must never invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

rubric.criterion: Properly assesses weight and route in scenario response.
Correctly simulates decisions to request assistance in practical activity.
Selects correct quiz answer about handling limits.

items.source_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
items.learning_objective: Show proficiency in critical task steps to an authorized assessor before working independently, emphasizing safety and privacy.
items.practical_activity: Perform a critical IT task (e.g., system access procedure) under observation by an authorized assessor who verifies each critical safety and privacy step is followed correctly.
items.lesson: Employees need to demonstrate the essential steps of their role tasks to an authorized assessor before working independently. If any critical safety or privacy step is missed, a numerical score cannot compensate; demonstrating full competence is mandatory. This ensures protection of systems and compliance with privacy standards.
checklist: Identify all critical steps of the assigned IT task.
Schedule a session with an authorized assessor.
Perform the task demonstrating all critical safety and privacy steps.
Obtain assessor confirmation of competence prior to independent work.

scenario.prompt: Your authorized assessor notes you skipped a privacy verification step. How should you proceed?
scenario.expected_response: Acknowledge the failed critical step cannot be compensated by score, and repeat the task correctly ensuring all critical steps including privacy verification are performed before independent work.

quiz.question: What happens if you fail a critical safety or privacy step during competence demonstration?
options: You must repeat the task demonstrating all critical steps.
A numerical score can compensate for the failure.
You can proceed with caution after assessment.
The step is ignored if other parts are correct.
quiz.explanation: A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step. The employee must demonstrate all critical steps before working independently.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

rubric.criterion: Acknowledges importance of all critical steps in scenario response.
Successfully performs all critical task steps in practical activity.
Chooses the correct quiz option about critical step failures.

items.source_quote: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
items.module_title: Recipient Verification and Data Disclosure Protocols
items.learning_objective: Verify requesters properly before disclosing shipment details, ensuring compliance with data privacy policies.
items.practical_activity: Practice following the approved workflow to verify a requester via simulated requests. Identify when to withhold recipient details despite having the shipment number.
items.lesson: Employees must always verify the requester using the approved workflow before sharing shipment information. Simply having a shipment number does not grant authorization to disclose recipient addresses or contacts. This protocol protects recipient privacy and company data security.
checklist: Review the approved workflow for requester verification.
Use the workflow to verify identity of requesters in simulated scenarios.
Confirm authorization before disclosing any shipment details beyond shipment numbers.
Withhold recipient address and contact info unless full verification is complete.

scenario.prompt: A person calls requesting recipient address but only provides the shipment number. How do you respond?
scenario.expected_response: Politely inform them that the shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure and that you must verify their identity through the approved workflow before sharing recipient details.

quiz.question: What must be done before disclosing recipient address or contact details?
options: Verify the requester using the approved workflow.
Provide details if the shipment number is given.
Disclose details if the requester sounds familiar.
Ignore privacy rules if the shipment number matches.
quiz.explanation: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.

rubric.criterion: Correctly explains verification procedure in scenario response.
Demonstrates use of approved workflow in practical activity.
Answers quiz identifying correct verification protocol.

items.source_quote: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.
items.learning_objective: Understand how to effectively communicate routine process frustrations and propose improvements to management respectfully and constructively.
items.practical_activity: Simulate a private conversation with your manager where you identify a specific process frustration and suggest an improvement with a supporting example.
items.lesson: Providing constructive feedback helps improve processes and working conditions. Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager, rather than publicly or via inappropriate channels. It is important to not only point out the problem but also to suggest a specific improvement supported by a clear example. This approach fosters open communication and continuous improvement within the team.
checklist: Identify a routine process frustration relevant to your IT role
Schedule a private meeting or conversation with your manager
Describe the frustration clearly and respectfully
Suggest a specific improvement backed by an example

scenario.prompt: You notice that the process for logging support tickets often causes delays. How would you communicate this to your manager?
scenario.expected_response: I would schedule a private meeting with my manager and explain that the current ticket logging process can delay responses. Then I would suggest a specific improvement, such as implementing a simplified ticket form or automated priority tagging, providing an example of how this helped in a previous role or team.

quiz.question: What is the recommended way to address routine process frustrations according to the policy?
options: Discuss them openly with the whole team during meetings

items.source_quote: The IT Support Engineer must assign only the approved role permissions and record any time-limited exception with expiry and approving owner. Administrative access must not be the default.

Assign only the permissions approved for that role.

Ensure administrative access is not assigned by default.

items.source_quote: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.

Refer to FAQs only after consulting policy, SOP, and role guides.

Notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 minutes of discovery.

Submit the official notification record as soon as practical after initial actions.

rubric.criterion: Demonstrates timely notification within 15 minutes in the scenario response.

items.lesson: New employees must complete their core orientation within 2 working days of joining the company. If the session is cancelled, promptly notify HR to arrange a replacement.
Ensure you complete orientation no later than the 2 working day deadline.

rubric.criterion: Explains importance of completing orientation within 2 working days.

matrix_snapshot.title: Handbook acknowledgement

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled repository
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Accidental disclosure
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

matrix_snapshot.title: Respectful conduct
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

matrix_snapshot.title: Knowledge assessment
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

matrix_snapshot.title: Attendance correction
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Version replacement
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Single incident owner
matrix_snapshot.text: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

matrix_snapshot.title: Temporary export removal
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted work
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

matrix_snapshot.title: Manual handling
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

matrix_snapshot.title: Practical competence
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

matrix_snapshot.title: Recipient verification
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.

matrix_snapshot.title: Constructive feedback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled copies
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must record document ID, owner, version, approval role and effective date before release. An unapproved draft must not be used to assign mandatory training.

matrix_snapshot.title: Approved fallback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.

matrix_snapshot.title: Verify recovery identity
matrix_snapshot.text: The IT Support Engineer must verify the account holder through the approved recovery workflow before resetting credentials. They must never ask the user to disclose an existing password or authentication code.

matrix_snapshot.title: Suspicious content
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.

matrix_snapshot.title: Screen lock
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.

requirements.text: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
requirements.title: Practical competence

requirements.text: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
requirements.title: Recipient verification

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.
requirements.title: Constructive feedback

requirements.text: Document owners must record document ID, owner, version, approval role and effective date before release. An unapproved draft must not be used to assign mandatory training.
requirements.title: Controlled copies

requirements.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.
requirements.title: Approved fallback

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer must verify the account holder through the approved recovery workflow before resetting credentials. They must never ask the user to disclose an existing password or authentication code.
requirements.title: Verify recovery identity

requirements.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.
requirements.title: Suspicious content

requirements.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.
requirements.title: Screen lock

requirements.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.
requirements.title: Continuity activation

requirements.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.
requirements.title: Planned absence notice

requirements.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Non retaliation

requirements.text: Employees must stop work and use the signed evacuation route when the alarm sounds. They must report to the assembly point and must not re-enter until the incident lead authorizes it.
requirements.title: Emergency evacuation

requirements.text: Employees hosting a visitor must arrange registration, a visible visitor pass and an escort in restricted areas. Visitors must not use employee access credentials.
requirements.title: Visitor escort

requirements.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.
requirements.title: Privacy requests

requirements.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.
requirements.title: Minimum fallback data

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to complete optional phishing simulations and discuss the warning signs with IT after the exercise.
requirements.title: Security practice

requirements.text: Employees must not operate powered warehouse equipment without documented authorization and task-specific training. Observing another operator does not grant authorization.
requirements.title: Restricted equipment

requirements.text: HR must retain onboarding acknowledgements, assessment attempts and readiness decisions for 24 months after the employee leaves the company, unless a preservation hold applies.
requirements.title: Training retention

requirements.text: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data. Personal storage services must not receive company files.
requirements.title: Approved devices

requirements.text: Employees must transfer open tasks, critical deadlines and escalation contacts to the designated cover before planned absence. Customer personal data must remain in approved systems.
requirements.title: Shift handover

requirements.text: Employees may propose a simpler fallback step after a rehearsal, provided the proposal preserves privacy, traceability and independent approval.
requirements.title: Continuity improvements

requirements.text: Employees must declare any offered gift valued above PKR 1,000 to HR before accepting it. Cash and cash-equivalent gifts are prohibited at any value; splitting a gift does not avoid this rule.
requirements.title: Gift declaration

requirements.text: Assigned record owners must reconcile fallback entries within 1 working day of restoration, resolve mismatches and dispose of temporary copies according to POL-06 and POL-07.
requirements.title: Fallback reconciliation

requirements.text: Employees must use fictional or irreversibly anonymized customer examples in training and demonstrations. Replacing a name alone does not anonymize a record containing a real telephone number or address.
requirements.title: Training data

requirements.text: Employees must obtain Managing Director approval before representing the company publicly or publishing customer-related material. Personal accounts must not disclose internal records.
requirements.title: Public statements

requirements.text: Employees must record actual events and must not fabricate delivery attempts, training completion, assessment results or approvals. Corrections must retain the original entry and the reason for amendment.
requirements.title: Accurate records

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer must record affected service, change, approver and rollback action for support work that changes configuration. Emergency changes require incident-lead authorization and subsequent documentation.
requirements.title: Record support changes

requirements.text: Responders must preserve relevant logs, messages and event identifiers without modifying originals. Evidence access must be restricted to the response team and a preservation hold applied where necessary.
requirements.title: Evidence preservation

requirements.text: Employees must use the confidential HR channel to report misconduct. If the concern involves HR, the report must go directly to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Confidential reporting

requirements.text: Employees must obtain recorded approval before taking planned leave. Submission alone is not approval, and employees must not approve their own request.
requirements.title: Approval before absence

requirements.text: Employees may select an optional development topic after agreeing the time allocation with their manager; optional learning must not delay mandatory training.
requirements.title: Personal development

requirements.text: Employees must transfer personal data only through approved company systems to authorized recipients. Personal messaging accounts and publicly accessible links are prohibited.
requirements.title: Approved transfer

requirements.text: Record owners must retain routine delivery-event records for 180 calendar days after case closure. A documented preservation hold overrides routine deletion until the hold is formally released.
requirements.title: Routine operational retention

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer must revoke employee access at the approved exit effective time and confirm completion to HR. An urgent termination notice requires immediate revocation and incident escalation if access remains active.
requirements.title: Revoke departing access

requirements.text: Employees must refer records with no applicable retention category to the Operations Manager before deletion. They must not infer a deadline from an unrelated record type.
requirements.title: Retention uncertainty

requirements.text: Teams are encouraged to rehearse one incident scenario each month and document a specific improvement to the response procedure.
requirements.title: Response rehearsal

requirements.text: HR must assign an onboarding plan based on role, experience, location and applicable requirements. Prior experience may change practice difficulty but must not remove mandatory acknowledgements.
requirements.title: Individual plan

requirements.text: Employees must access and collect only the customer fields needed for an assigned task. Full identity documents must not be requested for routine parcel tracking.
requirements.title: Minimum necessary data

requirements.text: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
requirements.title: Incident record

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer must confirm MFA, screen lock and approved-device controls before handing over an account or device, following POL-05.
requirements.title: Enable security controls

requirements.text: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.
requirements.title: Outage checkpoints

requirements.text: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
requirements.title: Record correction

requirements.text: Employees must pause the affected activity and ask the document owner when two equally authoritative instructions conflict or a necessary limit is missing. The owner must record the resolution before work resumes.
requirements.title: Unclear requirements

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss anticipated leave early so teams can plan coverage before a formal request is submitted.
requirements.title: Calendar planning

requirements.text: Managers must confirm required operational coverage before approving concurrent absences. If coverage cannot be arranged, the manager must record the reason and discuss alternative dates.
requirements.title: Minimum coverage

requirements.text: Employees must activate multifactor authentication before accessing email, remote access or systems holding customer records. IT must provide an approved recovery method rather than disabling the requirement.
requirements.title: Multifactor authentication

requirements.text: Record owners must use approved disposal methods and retain a disposal log identifying category, date range, authorization and completion date. Disposal must not expose readable personal data.
requirements.title: Secure disposal

requirements.text: Employees must disclose a personal or financial relationship with a merchant or supplier before participating in its selection, payment or complaint decision. The manager must assign an independent decision-maker.
requirements.title: Personal interests

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer may publish an approved self-service guide for recurring issues, excluding secrets and privileged operational details.
requirements.title: Improve support guidance

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to suggest improvements to workstation layout or parcel movement after discussing them with the supervisor.
requirements.title: Safety suggestions

requirements.text: Reviewers must verify required evidence before recording completion. Reading a module alone does not demonstrate practical competence or substitute for a required policy acknowledgement.
requirements.title: Completion integrity

requirements.text: Employees must record near misses even when no injury or damage occurs. The supervisor must assign a corrective action owner and verify completion.
requirements.title: Near misses

requirements.text: HR must record each employee role, department, joining date and reporting manager before assigning onboarding. A temporary role change requires a recorded start date, end date and additional requirements.
requirements.title: Role assignment

requirements.text: The incident lead must obtain an IT health check and an operational sample check before declaring normal service restored. A login screen alone is not evidence of end-to-end recovery.
requirements.title: Recovery verification

requirements.text: Employees must obtain IT approval before installing software or browser extensions on company devices. IT must verify business purpose and permitted access before approval.
requirements.title: Software installation

requirements.text: Employees entering marked warehouse handling zones must wear the posted protective equipment. The supervisor must stop the task if suitable equipment is unavailable.
requirements.title: Personal protective equipment

requirements.text: Employees must store API keys and service credentials only in approved secret storage and must not include them in source repositories, screenshots, training examples or support tickets.
requirements.title: Secrets handling

requirements.text: Only the incident lead or a designated spokesperson may issue incident updates to merchants or customers. Updates must distinguish confirmed impact from investigation assumptions.
requirements.title: External communication

requirements.text: Employees may suggest removal of unnecessary personal-data fields from forms, reports or dashboards to the relevant process owner.
requirements.title: Privacy improvements

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer must assign only the approved role permissions and record any time-limited exception with expiry and approving owner. Administrative access must not be the default.
requirements.title: Apply least privilege

requirements.text: Employees must classify an incident as critical when it involves immediate physical danger, suspected exposure of customer data or complete loss of dispatch capability. Where severity is uncertain, they must escalate as critical pending review.
requirements.title: Severity classification

requirements.text: Employees must check shipment and transaction identifiers before entering recovered work into the restored system. Potential duplicates must be held for review rather than posted again.
requirements.title: Duplicate prevention

requirements.text: Training managers must distribute learning across Day 1, Week 1, Week 2 and First 30 Days. Mandatory operational deadlines and prerequisites take priority over a convenient stage label.
requirements.title: Learning stages

requirements.text: Employees must report a non-urgent safety concern before the end of the current shift. An immediate danger requires stopping the activity and alerting the shift supervisor at once.
requirements.title: Safety concern reporting

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer must perform a monthly access review with managers and remove unapproved or expired permissions after recording the decision.
requirements.title: Review permissions

requirements.text: HR must restrict medical or other sensitive absence details to authorized People Operations staff. Operational managers receive only information needed to arrange work.
requirements.title: Sensitive absence details

requirements.text: The Operations Manager must identify scope, owner and start date when issuing a preservation hold. Record owners must suspend scheduled deletion for the named records until written release.
requirements.title: Preservation holds

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to arrange a weekly discussion with an experienced colleague during the first month to clarify workflows and identify useful practice.
requirements.title: Onboarding buddy

requirements.text: The incident lead must record recovery evidence, outstanding risks and corrective action owners before closure. The Operations Manager must review critical incidents within 2 working days after restoration.
requirements.title: Incident closure

requirements.text: The IT Support Engineer must verify employee identity, current role and manager approval before provisioning access. A support message without an approved request is insufficient.
requirements.title: Validate access request

requirements.text: Employees must use individually assigned accounts and must not share passwords or authentication codes. Service accounts require a named IT owner and must not be used for routine interactive work.
requirements.title: Individual accounts

requirements.text: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
requirements.title: Authoritative instructions

requirements.text: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
requirements.title: Critical escalation

requirements.text: Employees must complete core orientation within 2 working days of joining. HR must schedule a replacement session within that deadline if the original session is cancelled.
requirements.title: Core orientation
